changes: original_meaning 以第一个实词古英语 wyrd 的 gloss 记录为「命运」（现行首站取印欧词根『转』的 gloss，词根冒充，已改；『转→成为→命运』的理据写入 mechanism_sentence）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline/Wiktionary 编年重建三站（命运 → 约 1400 年 weird sisters → 1820 年奇怪义），how 写明现代义并非由古英语词直接演变、而是经短语与舞台形象中介的关键事实。
evidence: Etymonline: "weird (adj.) c. 1400, \"having power to control fate,\" in weird sisters, from weird (n.) \"force that sets events in motion or determines their course; what is destined to befall one;\" from Old English wyrd \"fate, chance, fortune; destiny; the Fates.\" The modern senses developed from weird sisters, not immediately from the Old English word, which is etymologically \"that which comes.\""

Etymonline: "The sense of \"uncanny, supernatural\" developed from Middle English use of weird sisters for the three Fates, Parcae, or Norns... They were portrayed as odd or frightening in appearance, as in \"Macbeth\" (especially in 18th and 19th century productions). The modern adjectival use, without sisters, emerged early 19c.... The weakened meaning \"odd-looking, strange, disturbingly different\" followed (1820)."

Wiktionary: "Obsolete by the 16th century in standard English. Its reintroduction is due to Shakespeare, who borrowed Scots 'weird sister(s)', denoting the Fates of classical mythology, for the witches in his play Macbeth."
weird.mechanism_sentence: weird 本是古英语 wyrd「命运」（与德语 werden「成为」同根——命运，就是将要成为的事）：这个词在标准英语里本已过时，靠莎士比亚《麦克白》里的命运三女巫翻红，先染上「超自然的诡异」，1820 年再弱化成泛泛的「奇怪」。

semantic_path.how: 形容词生于短语：约 1400 年 weird sisters 指纺织命运的诺恩三女神，weird 是『能左右命运的』；女神们在舞台上（尤其《麦克白》18–19 世纪的演法里）被扮作阴森可怖的女巫——『超自然、诡异』的色彩由此附着到词上。
semantic_path.meaning: （掌控命运的）；诡异的，超自然的

semantic_path.how: 再弱化一级：19 世纪初 weird 脱离 sisters 单独作形容词，约 1820 年滑到泛泛的『古怪的、异样的、令人不安地不同』——词库今义即此，从命运女神到日常怪事，走了四百年。

changes: original_meaning 保留「小麦」（古英语 hwǣte 的见载义，核对无误）；本条属守恒词，补丁以核对型规格处理。
semantic_path 第二站 how 以得名理据（与 white 同根、指谷粒麦粉之白）与颜色义的年代（1915 年）充实，替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "Middle English whete, from Old English hwæte \"wheat,\" from Proto-Germanic *hwaitjaz... The word is etymologically, \"that which is white\" (in reference to the color of the grain or the meal), from PIE *kwoid-yo-, suffixed variant form of root *kweid-, *kweit- \"to shine\" (see white; and compare Welsh gwenith \"wheat,\" related to gwenn \"white\"). As a name for a pale gold color like ripe wheat, it is attested by 1915."
wheat.mechanism_sentence: wheat 与 white 是同根亲戚：麦粒与麦粉的「白」，就是这株谷物得名的原因——从古英语 hwǣte 到今天，它的词义一步没挪，守着这片田。

semantic_path.how: 守恒的实据：从古英语到现代英语，wheat 的所指（这种谷物及其植株）从未分化或转移，可考的旁支只有 1915 年的色彩名义『熟麦的淡金色』——词库今义即首站本义。

changes: original_meaning 按古英语 hwīnan 的 gloss 改为「呼啸（穿过空气）」：现行字段把动词在不同主语下的用法（猛冲、尖叫、呜咽）堆作原义，其中『呜咽』属另一词形 hwinsian 与后起义。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（1520 年代抱怨义、1690 年代发嗲声调义）写明拟声词的所指迁移。
evidence: Etymonline: "whine (v.) \"make low, protracted sounds expressive of distress, etc.,\" Middle English whinen, from Old English hwinan \"to whiz, hiss, or whistle through the air\" (only of arrows), also hwinsian (in reference to the whimpering of dogs), from Proto-Germanic *hwinison... It is ultimately of imitative origin"
Etymonline: "The meaning \"complain in a feeble way\" is attested by 1520s. The transitive sense of \"utter in a thin, plaintive way\" is by 1690s."
Oxford: "Old English hwīnan 'whistle through the air', related to whinge."
whine.mechanism_sentence: whine 是个拟声词：古英语 hwīnan 是箭划破空气的尖啸——后来这声响从箭上转到了喉咙里，成了狗的哀鸣和人有气无力的抱怨（1520 年代）。

semantic_path.how: 声音换了发声体（拟声词的所指迁移）：中古英语 whine（及古英语旁形 hwinsian）先用于狗的呜咽，1520 年代添『有气无力地抱怨』义，1690 年代添『以发嗲拖腔的声调说话』义——划破空气的尖声，成了拖长的怨声；词库今义即此。

changes: original_meaning 按古英语 hāl 的 gloss 改为「完整的；安然无恙的」，两义并重（现行只有『健康的』一半，丢了『完整』这半——而『完整』恰是现代义的直系祖先）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明双生义的主次易位、名词化年代（14 世纪末）与 wh- 拼写的来历（15 世纪初），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "whole (adj.) Middle English hole, from Old English hal \"entire, whole; unhurt, uninjured, safe; healthy, healed, sound; genuine, straightforward,\" from Proto-Germanic *haila- \"undamaged\"... from PIE *kailo- \"whole, uninjured, of good omen\" (see health). The spelling with wh- developed early 15c."
Etymonline: "whole (n.) \"entire body or company; the full amount,\" late 14c., hole, from whole (adj.)."
Wiktionary: "The spelling with wh-, attested since ca. 1400, represents an excrescent /w/... in the former case likely reinforced by a desire to disambiguate from hole."
whole.mechanism_sentence: whole 与 health、heal、holy 是一家人：古英语 hāl 一身兼着「完整」与「无伤、健康」两义——完好无损，所以一整个；15 世纪初，它还给自己添了个 wh- 的拼写帽子（也顺便和 hole 拉开距离）。

semantic_path.how: 双生义分了主次：hāl 的『健康、无伤』一支由 health、hale 等亲戚分担，whole 专攻『一整个、全体的』，14 世纪末生出名词『整体、全部』（词库今义）——拼写则在 15 世纪初添上 wh-。
